intro.title: Discover Stephen the Great Central Park
intro.description: Grădina Publică „Ștefan cel Mare și Sfânt" is the oldest park in Chișinău, established in 1818. It is an iconic relaxation spot in the heart of Moldova's capital, frequented by both locals and tourists. Walking along the shady alleys, you will discover historical monuments, decorative fountains, and a unique atmosphere of tranquility and greenery.

visitGuide.title: Visit Tips

knowledge.title: About Stephen the Great Central Park

sections.title: Historical Background
sections.content: The park was established in 1818 as the oldest park in Chișinău. Originally called "Public Garden", it was designed by German architect Johann F. W. Meinz. Throughout the centuries, the park has witnessed many historical events and undergone significant transformations while preserving its original charm.

sections.title: Geography & Layout
sections.content: The park is located in the city center on Ștefan cel Mare și Sfânt Boulevard. It is divided into several areas, including the famous "Alley of Classics" where 29 busts of celebrated Romanian writers and poets are placed. In the center stands the Stephen the Great statue, a symbol of the city.

sections.title: Cultural Significance
sections.content: As the "green lung" of Chișinău, the park is the preferred meeting place for locals. Cultural events, open-air concerts, and exhibitions are frequently organized here. It is a symbol of national identity and an indispensable resting place for capital residents.

sections.title: Ecology & Flora
sections.content: The garden hosts a wide variety of tree and shrub species, including centuries-old oaks, plane trees, linden trees, and conifers. The green landscape provides a refuge for various urban bird species, making it ideal for nature lovers.

officialManagement.title: About Stephen the Great Central Park
officialManagement.text: Grădina Publică „Ștefan cel Mare și Sfânt" is the oldest and most iconic park in Chișinău, being a perfect example of combining city history with nature. The area is co-managed by the Chișinău City Hall and local environmental protection departments for ecological conservation and daily management.

thingsToDo.title: Things to Do in Chișinău
thingsToDo.description: A practical Chișinău travel guide: top attractions, parks, museums, cathedrals, markets and wine experiences in Moldova's capital.
thingsToDo.intro: Chișinău, the capital of Moldova, is a compact, walkable city built around green boulevards and Soviet-era architecture. Most visitors base themselves in the centre, where Stephen the Great Central Park sits at the heart of the city. From here you can reach museums, cathedrals, markets and wine bars on foot or by a short trolleybus ride.

sections.title: Parks & green spaces
sections.content: Start with Stephen the Great Central Park, the oldest and most central park in the city. Other favourites include Valea Morilor (a lakeside park in the south-west), the Dendrarium with its collection of trees, and Parcul La Izvor near the exhibition centre. All are free to enter and pleasant for a stroll.

sections.title: Museums & history
sections.content: The National Museum of History of Moldova sits on 31 August 1989 Street, a short walk from the park, and holds archaeology, weapons and the famous 'Pommery' cellar exhibits. The National Museum of Ethnography and Natural History and the Pushkin Museum are also worth a visit.

sections.title: Cathedrals & monasteries
sections.content: The Nativity Cathedral and its belfry dominate the central square, while the nearby Căpriana and Hîncu monasteries make easy half-day trips outside the city for those interested in Orthodox heritage.

sections.title: Markets & food
sections.content: The Central Market (Piața Centrală) is the place to taste local produce, plăcinte (pastries), cheeses and brandy. Pair it with a walk along the pedestrianised stretch of Ștefan cel Mare Boulevard for cafés and people-watching.

sections.title: Wine experiences
sections.content: Moldova is one of the world's great wine countries. Underground cellars such as Cricova and Milestii Mici can be visited on guided tours from Chișinău, and many city wine bars pour indigenous varieties like Fetească Neagră and Rară Neagră.

parks.title: Parks in Chișinău
parks.description: Compare Chișinău's main parks — location, atmosphere and what each one is best for.
parks.intro: Chișinău is surprisingly green. Beyond Stephen the Great Central Park in the centre, the city has lakeside parks, botanical collections and quiet neighbourhood gardens. Here is how the main ones compare.

sections.title: Stephen the Great Central Park
sections.content: The most central and historic park, founded in 1818. Best for a quick walk, the Alley of Classics with 29 writers' busts, and the Stephen the Great monument. Flat, shaded and steps from the cathedral and museums.

sections.title: Valea Morilor
sections.content: A large lakeside park in the south-west with a promenade, fountains and a beach area. Best for longer walks, jogging and weekend picnics away from the centre.

sections.title: Dendrarium Park
sections.content: A botanical park managed by the Academy of Sciences with labelled trees and quiet alleys. Best for nature lovers and photography, with a small entry fee.

sections.title: Parcul La Izvor
sections.content: A modern park near the Moldexpo exhibition centre with a lake, playgrounds and open spaces. Good for families and events.

parkHistory.title: History of Stephen the Great Central Park
parkHistory.description: The story of Chișinău's oldest park: from the 1818 Public Garden to today's Alley of Classics.
parkHistory.intro: Grădina Publică „Ștefan cel Mare și Sfânt” is the oldest park in Chișinău and a living record of the city's changing identity. Its layout, monuments and trees have been shaped over more than two centuries.

sections.title: The 1818 Public Garden
sections.content: The park was laid out in 1818, shortly after Chișinău became the capital of Bessarabia, and was originally called the 'Public Garden' (Grădina Publică). It was designed by the German architect Johann F. W. Meinz as a formal green space for the new administrative centre.

sections.title: The Alley of Classics
sections.content: The park's signature feature is the Alley of Classics (Aleea Clasicilor), an open-air sculpture gallery of 29 busts honouring Romanian writers, poets and scholars. It was developed through the 20th century and remains a favourite meeting point.

sections.title: The Stephen the Great monument
sections.content: At the centre stands the equestrian monument to Stephen the Great (Ștefan cel Mare), the Moldavian prince who ruled in the 15th century. Unveiled in 1928, it has become the symbolic heart of the city and a common reference point for meetings.

sections.title: A modern urban park
sections.content: Today the park is co-managed by the Chișinău municipality and blends historic avenues with a cascade fountain, a summer open-air theatre and event spaces, remaining free and open to the public around the clock.

parkMap.title: Stephen the Great Central Park — Map & Entrances
parkMap.description: Where the park is, how to enter it, walking routes and nearby transport in central Chișinău.
parkMap.intro: The park occupies a rectangular block in the very centre of Chișinău, bordered by Ștefan cel Mare și Sfânt Boulevard to the north and adjacent central streets. It has several entrances, so you can step in from almost any side.

sections.title: Location
sections.content: The park sits at Ștefan cel Mare și Sfânt Boulevard 148, directly across from the Nativity Cathedral and the main pedestrian axis of the city. Its coordinates place it at the geographic centre of Chișinău's sightseeing loop.

sections.title: Entrances
sections.content: The main gates face Ștefan cel Mare Boulevard, but there are additional openings onto adjacent streets, making the park easy to enter whether you arrive from the cathedral, the boulevard or the surrounding blocks.

sections.title: Suggested walking route
sections.content: Enter from the boulevard, pause at the Stephen the Great monument, continue along the Alley of Classics to see the 29 busts, circle the cascade fountain and finish at the summer open-air theatre before exiting toward the cathedral square.

sections.title: Nearby attractions
sections.content: Just outside the park you will find the Nativity Cathedral, the National Museum of History of Moldova and the Central Market. The National Museum of History is a separate institution a few minutes' walk away and should not be confused with the park itself.

sections.title: Getting there
sections.content: The park is reachable on foot from anywhere in the centre. Numerous trolleybus and bus lines stop along Ștefan cel Mare Boulevard, and it is a short taxi or walk from the railway and bus stations.
